svg.title: German Unification, Annexed Alsace-Lorraine & Bismarck’s Two-Front Fear (1871–1890)
svg.desc: KS3 historical GIS atlas map of Western and Central Europe (1871–1890) showing the Unified German Empire, Prussia and the industrial Ruhr, the September 1870 Battle of Sedan, the 18 January 1871 Proclamation at the Palace of Versailles, annexed Alsace-Lorraine, and Chancellor Bismarck’s fear of a two-front war between France and Russia.

text.tspan: Unified Jan 1871 • Kingdom of Prussia Core
Bismarck’s steel, Krupp artillery & railway powerhouse
Napoleon III captured; French Second Empire collapses
German Empire proclaimed inside France’s Hall of Mirrors
Metz forts & iron ore (+ 5bn fine) seized
Sandwiched between France & Russia; Bismarck isolates France

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 9 ENQUIRY: CAUSES OF THE GREAT WAR
German Unification, Annexed Alsace-Lorraine & Bismarck’s Europe
Bismarck’s "Blood and Iron" wars united Germany at Versailles (Jan 1871), creating Europe’s strongest industrial and military power.
Seizing Alsace-Lorraine sparked lasting French Revanche, forcing Bismarck into alliances with Austria & Russia to avoid a two-front war.
